title: Dom Dolla Launches Good Fortune Records
summary: The superstar Australian DJ and producer unveils Good Fortune Records, which launches proper this Friday (Oct. 16) with its first release -- Torren Foot & rhys from the sticks’ “DANCE.”
contentText:
Dom Dolla , the superstar EDM DJ and producer can now add “label chief” to his resume.

The Australian artist today unveils Good Fortune Records, which launches proper this Friday (Oct. 16) with its first release, Torren Foot & rhys from the sticks’ “ DANCE .”

Good Fortune expands on a party series Dom created in 2024 to bring into the spotlight emerging and established artists, doing so in unique spaces and locations. Dom’s Good Fortune nights have kicked off in Melbourne, Los Angeles, New York, Miami, Detroit, London and Manchester, and featured performances and back-to-back sets with the likes of Solomun, Green Velvet, Tiga, Fcukers and Skream.

“After 20 years of DJing, I still find nothing more exciting than discovering new records that rip holes through a dance floor,” remarks Dom in a statement. “This week, I’m finally launching Good Fortune Records. A record label that began as a party brand I’ve been running events under for the last few years. A place where both new up and coming artists and established legends can come together and do what they do best.”

View this post on Instagram

Dom debuted “DANCE” in December 2025 when he played Sydney’s Allianz Stadium, marking the first time a homegrown DJ had filled a stadium in these parts.

When Dom established another record last month, with his hometown show at Melbourne’s Marvel Stadium , he dropped the track to some 60,000 fans. Torren has been teasing “DANCE” on socials over the past month, keeping a list of all the DJs playing it — a tally that includes the groundbreaking Docklands show where he joined Dom on stage for a performance. Dom has since played the track with Ketama at Head Trip Festival 2026 in California.

“It’s been a staple in my set for the last 12 months,” Dom enthuses.

There’s never a dull moment for Dom. Raised in Darwin, Dom (real name: Dominic Matheson) became a fixture on Melbourne’s club scene before taking his talents to the world.

Last year, he was nominated for a Grammy Award; won a slew of ARIA Awards, including the inaugural ARIA Global Impact Award; sold-out two nights at Madison Square Garden and ticked off a bucket list item when he released “No Room For A Saint,” the soundtrack for F1: The Movie . It’s been more of the same this year with an itinerary that has included major festival and headline shows across Asia, Latin and North America, the United Kingdom and Europe, a 13-week residency at Hï Ibiza, an extension of his residency at LIV Las Vegas, and new releases, including a remix of Puretone’s “Addicted To Bass” (dubbed “ Dom Dolla Relapse “).

Just two days after he performed at Marvel Stadium, Dom was on the ground of another Aussie stadium, the Melbourne Cricket Ground, where he made a cameo during Kylie Minogue’s halftime entertainment spot at the 2026 AFL Grand Final .
